name: agsl-plasma
title: AGSL plasma shader
summary: A full-canvas AGSL runtime shader that sums four sine fields into a flowing rainbow plasma, animated by binding iTime to continuousSec().
prompt: An animated psychedelic plasma background made with an AGSL shader that moves over time.
teaches: Attach an AGSL runtime shader to the paint with shader {agsl, uniforms}
Animate a shader by binding a float uniform to an expression such as continuousSec()
Pass a float2 uniform as a two-element array (iResolution [componentWidth(), componentHeight()])
Cover the canvas with a drawRect to componentWidth() × componentHeight() so the shader runs on every pixel
pitfalls: Uniform names in `uniforms` must match the AGSL declarations exactly; an undeclared uniform is ignored and a missing one stays 0
The shader only colours what is drawn with the paint: without the drawRect nothing appears

main receives canvas coordinates in pixels, not 0..1: normalise them with a resolution uniform (here iResolution, bound to componentWidth() and componentHeight(): a literal header size goes wrong as soon as the document is resized)
Bind iTime to continuousSec(), which keeps repainting; animationTime() alone never schedules a repaint, so the plasma would freeze
A shader bound to the clock repaints every frame: pin `clock` to compare renders

snippets.note: paint shader: AGSL source plus uniforms iResolution [componentWidth(), componentHeight()] and iTime = continuousSec()
a drawRect covering the component runs the shader on every pixel

check.describe: A saturated rainbow plasma covering the canvas; renders at 10:10:00 and 10:10:02 differ. Resized, the plasma still covers the whole canvas and its pattern scales with the height (iResolution follows the component size).
